thread.title: Apple’s stock rises, even with early HomePod reviews far from raves

title: Apple’s stock rises, even with early HomePod reviews far from raves
text:
Apple Inc. may not be selling as many iPhone Xs as Wall Street had expected, but the company got a nice boost in its latest quarter from its “other products” segment, which was up 36% from year earlier and counts the Apple Watch and AirPod earphones among its components.
This quarter, the company will be able to add a new item to that list: the delayed HomePod speaker, which finally becomes available Friday. Analysts aren’t expecting much from the device, given its high price point and Apple’s late entry to the market. And early reviewers, who published their initial HomePod thoughts Tuesday morning, seemed to echo these concerns, even as they praised the device’s sound quality.
Apple shares AAPL, +1.76% were up 1.1% near midday. 
The company announced the HomePod back in June, originally planning for a December launch. Once Apple pushed back the release, the device missed out on the holiday season, after already being years behind competing voice-controlled-speaker offerings from Amazon.com Inc AMZN, +1.19% and Google parent Alphabet Inc. GOOGL, -0.66% . This was a point noted by several reviewers. 
“At the talking speaker party, Apple’s HomePod isn’t just fashionably late — it’s late late,” wrote the Wall Street Journal’s Joanna Stern , who commented that Amazon and Google have already sold tens of millions of their own speakers.
Stern was among numerous reviewers who keyed in on the smart speaker’s lack of smarts. The device couldn’t provide an answer when she asked who the prime minister of England was, though it fared better when Stern sharpened her phrasing and asked about the prime minister of Great Britain instead. Speakers from Google and Amazon were able to answer both versions of the question. Another concern: “The HomePod has an iPhone processor and pairs with your iPhone — yet it can’t make a phone call? To use it as a speakerphone, you need to start the call on your iPhone then select the HomePod as an audio source.”
Brian X. Chen of the New York Times highlighted further shortcomings . Unlike its peers, the HomePod wasn’t able to hail an Uber, explain how to make pasta or add a calendar event. “Siri on HomePod is embarrassingly inadequate, even though that is the primary way you interact with it,” Chen wrote. “Siri is sorely lacking in capabilities compared with Amazon’s Alexa and Google’s Assistant. Siri doesn’t even work as well on HomePod as it does on the iPhone.”
Another key criticism cited by reviewers was Apple’s “walled garden” approach to compatibility. The HomePod “demands that you live entirely inside Apple’s ecosystem in a way that even Apple’s other products do not,” wrote Nilay Patel of the Verge . While Amazon and Google let you make Spotify your default music app on their devices, Apple won’t let you dictate commands for Spotify playback on the HomePod, he joined others in noting. You can AirPlay songs from Spotify or Pandora by physically tapping on them on your phone; otherwise, you’re limited to using Apple Music for voice controls. Streaming is a popular activity on smart speakers. Apple Music is still less popular than Spotify, and Apple is trying to drive more subscriptions to its music platform in order to boost its booming services segment.
Pandora Media Inc. P, -2.24% CEO Roger Lynch called Apple’s HomePod approach a “huge mistake” in an interview with MarketWatch last month.
One positive theme highlighted by reviewers was the device’s sound quality, however. “For a compact speaker, the HomePod offers big sound, and in testing I found it pretty much unflappable no matter what kind of music I threw its way,” wrote CNET’s Megan Wollerton . “It’s hard to say that about many speakers, regardless of size.” Overall, she found that the speaker sounded crisper than similarly high-end ones from Google and Sonos. The HomePod sells for $349, while Sonos offers two of its Sonos One devices for that price. The Google Home Max goes for $399.
In the end, sound quality wasn’t enough to sell reviewers on the Apple speaker. “That’s really the crux of it: the HomePod sounds incredible, but not so world-bendingly amazing that you should switch away from Spotify, or accept Siri’s frustrating limitations as compared to Alexa,” the Verge’s Patel concluded.
Apple shares are up 23% over the past 12 months, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, -0.25% , of which Apple is a component, is up 22%.
